scope: Float32 finite-seam coverage diagnostic; not a native Split comparison
openDefect: A rounded seam midpoint can leave an edge and materially distort coverage while both generated faces retain positive winding. The regression remains marked as an expected failure in tests/scan-split-finite-seams.test.ts.

discardedApproach.method: Reject when the vector sum of child face normals differs from the immediate refined face normal by more than one part per million.
discardedApproach.observation: The known distortion was rejected, but the retained original-scan face crossing also failed because a very small refined face had a relative difference of approximately 0.0004688. The existing full-source-face coverage test accepts that case.
discardedApproach.disposition: Removed the check; no arbitrary threshold or application behavior change was retained.

strictCollinearityProbe.method: In the Float32-only path, reject rounded midpoints whose edge determinants differ beyond double-precision arithmetic error; leave precise-coordinate output unchanged.
strictCollinearityProbe.observation: The material-distortion regression passed, but the retained original-scan crossing failed: its rounded midpoint is not exactly collinear even though the complete source-face coverage test accepts it.
strictCollinearityProbe.result: Candidate removed because it rejects an existing valid original-scan case; 86 tests passed and one failed.
strictCollinearityProbe.nextInvestigation: Carry the original source-face identity and coverage budget into seam validation or preserve precise coordinates throughout; do not use a strict local collinearity test as a substitute.

preciseOriginalFace.scope: The same original face and cutter through the precise finite candidate used by the shared operation, not a native comparison.
preciseOriginalFace.result: Positive winding and total projected source-face coverage pass to ten decimal places; the Float32 expected failure remains.

limitations: The Float32 helper defect remains unresolved. The current shared GUI/MCP finite mesh Split requests the separate precise-coordinate output mode.
Native Split behavior, full M2 acceptance and merge remain open.
